summary: Create a fresh ECMAScript RegExp object for every regular-expression literal evaluation.

target.notes: A literal may be compiled ahead of time, but each evaluation must produce a distinct stateful RegExp object with lastIndex initialized to 0.

semantics.engine: ECMAScript RegExp grammar and matching semantics

caveats: Do not cache and reuse the mutable RegExp object itself; global/sticky lastIndex would leak between evaluations.
.NET Regex grammar and matching semantics are not a general substitute for ECMAScript RegExp.

tests.name: literal state is not shared
tests.input: function f(){ return /a/g; } const a=f(); a.test('a'); const b=f(); console.log(a.lastIndex,b.lastIndex);
